newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's o/n rates end lower on abundant funds.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's o/n rates end lower on abundant funds.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interest rates continued to drop on Friday as funds from matured reverse repo rates flowed onto the market, dealers said.
The overnight rates closed at 20 percent, down from Thursday's finish of 20.375 percent.
The National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) half percentage point repo rate cuts, carried out three weeks ago, weighed on overnight interest rate levels, dealers said.

Before the repo cuts, substantial funds flowed into one-month reverse repo deals and returning onto the market last week, they pushed the overnight rates down to 18 percent, triggering a new wave of placing money into reverse repo deals for one week at 20.25 percent, dealers said.
These one-week reverse repo contracts matured this week, flooding the market with fresh funds and pushing overnight rates down again, they said.
Dealers added they did not foresee factors to reduce market liquidity substantially in the near future and next week the rates may go down to levels between 18 and 19 percent again.

Sandor Tolonics of Commerzbank said the NBH had given indications that it wanted to keep its interest rates steady but part of market players still expected a cut in the 20.75 percent one-month reverse repo rate.
